thread:
jordan: Heads-up — dashboards started showing a gap in token-level latency and kvcache metrics for a subset of routes (chat.generate, chat.streaming) around 09:02 UTC. token_latency_ms and kvcache_hits are flatlined for ~6m while request volume stayed normal. :eyes:
anya: Oh no. Any exporter errors in the logs? StatsD/OTel?
sam: I pulled the exporter pod logs. Seeing repeated lines: "statsd: buffer write failed: write: no space left on device" and OTLP exporter warnings about batch timeout. pasted a snippet: ```
[2026-03-16T09:02:11Z] statsd: buffer write failed: write: no space left on device
[2026-03-16T09:02:12Z] otel_exporter: batch timeout exceeded, dropping 42 metrics
```
jordan: That matches the time window. The runtime trace shows kernel selection flapping (a recent change to prefer quantized kernels for long-prefix traffic), which might have increased per-token CPU contention and caused exporter queues to back up.
lee: Hmm, I wonder if the kvcache emitter runs on the same CPU core as kernel selection path and we overflow the StatsD UDP buffer under heavy autoshard batching. Could explain missing kvcache_hits specifically.
anya: Can we confirm which hosts/pods were affected? Are only Dedicated pods or also Hosted?
sam: A quick grep: affected pods are runtime-pool-qa-3/4/7 in eu-west-1 (shared infra with Dedicated). Hosted pool untouched.
metrics-bot: Alert fired: metrics-drop-eu-west-1 at 2026-03-16T09:02:15Z — severity=warning — routes=[chat.generate,chat.streaming] — missing_fields=[kvcache_hits,token_latency_ms]
jordan: I ran a flamegraph on runtime-pool-qa-3 at 09:03 and saw exporter flush task stuck behind kernel selection work. Short excerpt: 
- runtime.loop -> kernel_selector.select_best_kernel (40%)
- runtime.loop -> batching.coalescer (20%)
- metrics.emitter.flush (2%) but queue len peaked at 1200
sam: Uploaded the profiler svg: https://ci.internal/redwood/profiles/1778005432/runtime-pool-qa-3.svg
lee: Proposed immediate mitigation: (1) increase StatsD UDP recv buffer on nodes (net.core.rmem_max & rmem_default), (2) reduce exporter max_batch_size from 500 -> 200, (3) throttle kernel-selector concurrency for late-night rollout.
anya: Agree on (1) + (2) as quick hotfix. Who can patch the daemonset?
lee: I'll do a rolling daemonset bump for node sysctl and smaller exporter config. Plan: bump on one AZ, wait 10m, then roll.
jordan: Small note — kv cache TTL churn also spiked right before the gap. I suspect a reconfiguration of prefix caching (we lowered prefix TTL to favor freshness) that caused more KV churn and extra emit traffic. CC: @sam to cross-check config change history.
sam: Confirmed — config PR #4802 that reduced kvcache.prefix_ttl from 15m -> 2m merged 2026-03-16T08:50 by infra-ops. That increased kvcache eviction rate ~x4 in our test window.
metrics-bot: config-change detected: infra-ops/PR#4802 merged by infra-ops at 2026-03-16T08:50:11Z — changed kvcache.prefix_ttl=120s
jordan: OK, root cause hypothesis: TTL change -> higher kvcache churn -> more metrics emitted -> exporter queue/backpressure -> dropped metrics for kvcache_* and token_latency_ms (emitted by same emitter) because of buffer overflow. Kernel selection perf regression made emit latency worse, magnifying problem.
anya: What's the plan for backfilling the missing metrics? We need token-level latency for the affected 6m window across eu-west-1.
lee: We'll run a metrics backfill job from the raw event sink. Backfill command (dry-run first): ```
python infra/metrics/backfill.py 
  --start=2026-03-16T09:02:00Z 
  --end=2026-03-16T09:08:00Z 
  --routes=chat.generate,chat.streaming 
  --tags=kvcache,token_latency 
  --dry-run
```
jordan: After dry-run looks OK, we'll run for real with --job-id=backfill-1778005432. Note: backfill needs to rehydrate per-route token breakdowns and inject into metrics store with correct timestamps (no TTL collision).
sam: I already extracted raw event fragments for runtime-pool-qa-3/4/7 and stored them under s3://redwood-internal/metrics-backfill/1778005432/ — permission granted to eng-infra.
anya: Thanks. Also we should add a dashboard alert to trigger earlier if exporter queue length > 500 and kvcache_evictions > 200/s.
lee: Will add two alert rules and a per-route KPI card showing token_latency_ms broken down by kernel selection tag (serving.kernel.type). That should help catch future corner cases.
metrics-bot: Backfill job queued: backfill-1778005432 by jordan — status=queued
infra-cd-bot: Deployment started: infra-exporter config bump (reduce batch_size) — rollout id infra-roll-8271 — target: runtime-exporter-daemonset — start=2026-03-16T09:22:00Z
jordan: Post-rollback note for the kernel selector change — we should revert the preference patch or add a safety cap. I'll open a PR to add a soft cap on kernel selection concurrency and a fallback to previous kernel if emitter queue > threshold.
sam: Forensics checklist I'm doing: (1) confirm dropped metric counts from exporter logs, (2) reconcile emitted counts vs backfilled events, (3) validate per-token latency after backfill, (4) adjust kvcache TTL config if needed.
lee: After a partial roll we saw exporter errors drop to zero on runtime-pool-qa-3. Monitoring now shows kvcache_hits recovering and token_latency_ms reappearing in dashboards. :thumbsup:
anya: Once backfill completes, let's run evals on a sample of traces to ensure quality hasn't regressed due to kernel change.
jordan: Thanks all. Action items: lee deploy sysctl+exporter config (in progress), sam prepare backfill artifacts (done), anya add alerts/dashboard cards, jordan PR for safety caps. Follow up in this thread with job id and post-backfill verification results.
lee: Backfill started for real: job=backfill-1778005432-run1 at 2026-03-16T09:35:10Z
metrics-bot: Backfill job update: backfill-1778005432-run1 — progress=25% — eta=10m
sam: Backfill sanity check: rehydrated token samples match original request traces for a sample set (n=200) — mean token_latency delta = +1.2ms (within expected).
jordan: Verified dashboards show token_latency_ms restored for the window. Closing the incident after a 1h monitoring window if no regressions. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
